source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section IV.3 (mounding/hilling the base)
text: Mounding soil up around the base of each banana clump after weeding is an important practice because it covers and protects the shallow surface roots that can otherwise become exposed by rain, irrigation, or routine field work. Since banana roots are naturally close to the surface and easily damaged when left bare, keeping a small soil mound built up around the base helps the plant stay anchored, protects roots from drying out or physical damage, and supports overall plant vigor going into the fruiting stage.
